name: Momentum_OS
summary: Momentum OS is a personal productivity web app that brings tasks, habits, goals, notes, a journal, a calendar, focus timers, academic tracking and career tracking into one place. It uses game-like touches such as levels, XP, streaks, a cat intro and a cozy desk view, and it offers AI help that turns typed or spoken sentences into tasks, goals and other entries. It is built with Next.js, and its data is saved in the browser first and then synced to an online Supabase database. The repository also holds a set of design helper scripts for AI tools (in .agents) and a folder of one-off test scripts (in scratch).
who_its_for: Mainly students, early-career professionals and builders who want one app to manage studies, job or internship applications, hackathons, habits and goals. The app has a persona setting for student, professional or builder, which changes its wording.
how_it_runs: It runs as a Next.js web app, started with the commands in package.json. The browser keeps a local copy of the data, the Supabase cloud database stores the synced copy, and two server endpoints send text and audio to Groq for AI and speech-to-text. How it is deployed is unclear from the summaries.

areas.name: src/components
areas.summary: All the on-screen pieces of the app, grouped by feature: tasks, habits, goals, notes, journal, calendar, career, academic, analytics, focus, dashboard, settings, login and shared buttons and cards.
areas.why: This is what the user actually sees and clicks.
areas.debug_tips: Find the folder named after the screen that looks wrong. Most screens read their data from the central store, so a wrong number may come from the store or the helper functions rather than the screen.

areas.name: .agents
areas.summary: Helper scripts and tests for AI design tools: brand colors, design tokens, slide building, logo, icon and corporate identity pictures, Tailwind setup and style search.
areas.why: They keep the look of the app and marketing material consistent, but they are not part of the running app.
areas.debug_tips: Problems here show up only when running these scripts directly. The Gemini based generators likely need an API key, though the summaries do not say where it is kept.

areas.name: scratch
areas.summary: Manual one-off scripts for checking the database, the AI parsing and the sign-up behavior, plus environment printouts. Some of the checks are fixed text rather than real tests.
areas.why: They help the developer confirm that the cloud database and AI features work.
areas.debug_tips: Several scripts talk to the live database and write or delete records, so be careful running them. The environment printing scripts show parts of secret keys, so do not share their output.

areas.name: src/utils
areas.summary: Small helper code: grade average math, the AI helper logic (offline and Groq based), analytics scores, CSV export, starting data, persona wording and generated sounds.
areas.why: It holds the calculations and AI switching logic that many screens rely on.
areas.debug_tips: For wrong scores, grades or AI results, check the matching helper file. The AI helper chooses between an offline mode and a server mode, so check which one is in use.

areas.name: src/app
areas.summary: The app's entry point: the page that picks the login, intro or main layout, the shared page frame, the global styles and the two server endpoints for AI and speech-to-text.
areas.why: Every visit starts here, and the AI endpoints are the bridge to Groq.
areas.debug_tips: If AI or voice features fail, look at the two route files and check the Groq key is set. If the wrong screen shows at start, look at page.tsx.

areas.name: (root files)
areas.summary: Project settings files: the library and command list, Next.js, TypeScript and PostCSS setup.
areas.why: They control how the app is built and started.
areas.debug_tips: Build or startup errors usually trace back to package.json or the TypeScript settings. The tsconfig summary only says it points to two other files, which are not listed.

areas.name: src/lib
areas.summary: Code that connects to the browser's local database and to Supabase, including a queue of changes waiting to be sent to the cloud.
areas.why: It is what makes the app work offline and sync later.
areas.debug_tips: If data does not appear online, check whether Supabase is configured and whether changes are stuck in the local queue.

areas.name: src/store
areas.summary: The central memory of the app: one store holds all tasks, habits, notes and goals and saves them locally and to the cloud, and another handles who is signed in.
areas.why: Nearly every screen reads and writes through these two files.
areas.debug_tips: If something saves but then disappears or does not sync, start with useMomentumStore.ts. Login problems point to useAuthStore.ts.

areas.name: supabase
areas.summary: Two database setup scripts that create the cloud tables with row-level security, add a persona setting, set the coins default and make a profile for each new sign-up.
areas.why: The cloud data cannot be stored correctly unless these tables and rules exist.
areas.debug_tips: If saves fail or a new account has no profile, confirm both migrations were applied. Row-level security can silently block access.

areas.name: src
areas.summary: A single top-level stylesheet that sets the dark warm theme, scrollbars, frosted panels, glow effects and a pulsing animation.
areas.why: It shapes the overall look, though a similar stylesheet also lives in src/app.
areas.debug_tips: If styling looks off, check both this file and src/app/globals.css, since it is unclear which one wins.

areas.name: src/types
areas.summary: One file that describes the shape of every kind of data in the app and the allowed choices for each.
areas.why: It is the shared dictionary that keeps the store, screens and database consistent.
areas.debug_tips: If a field is missing or a value is rejected, compare it with this file and with the database tables.

readiness.summary: Top three fixes: add automated tests for the app itself, add CI plus a written deploy and rollback process, and add error tracking and logging. Next, verify Supabase access rules and scan git history for secrets.

checks.question: Does the app build and start with one documented command?
checks.evidence: `package.json` has `dev`, `build` and `start` scripts, and the README names Next.js 15. The visible README excerpt shows no install or run command, and the build was not run.
checks.next_step: Add a Getting Started section to `README.md` with `npm install`, `npm run dev`, and the required env vars.

checks.question: Are there automated tests, and do they pass?
checks.evidence: The only test files are under `.agents/skills/` (Python tests for design tooling). There are no tests for the app itself and no `test` script in `package.json`. Not checked: whether any tests pass, because tests were not run.
checks.next_step: Add a test runner such as Vitest and tests for the core stores (habits, tasks, Life Score), then add a `test` script.

checks.question: When something goes wrong, does the app show a clear message instead of crashing or failing silently?
checks.evidence: Not checked: the evidence has no error boundary or `error.tsx` information. The scan found 0 swallowed errors, which is a good sign but does not show that users see clear messages.
checks.next_step: Add `app/error.tsx` and `app/global-error.tsx`, and show user-facing messages on failed saves and imports.

checks.question: Does it check what people type or upload before using it?
checks.evidence: The scan found 80 input-validation matches in 28 files, so some validation exists. The evidence does not show whether JSON import and uploads are validated against a schema.
checks.next_step: Validate JSON backup imports with a schema (e.g. zod) before loading them into state.

checks.question: Are passwords and API keys kept out of the code and out of git history?
checks.evidence: No env files are tracked, `.gitignore` mentions `.env`, and a scan of HEAD found 0 secret-looking strings. Git history was not scanned.
checks.next_step: Run a history scan (gitleaks or trufflehog) and add a `.env.example`.

checks.question: Can only the right people see and change things (sign-in and permissions)?
checks.evidence: There are 38 auth/session/permission matches in 16 files, and `supabase/migrations` suggests a Supabase backend. The README describes a client-side Zustand app with offline JSON backup. The evidence does not show row-level security policies or server-side route protection.
checks.next_step: Confirm RLS policies exist in `supabase/migrations` for every user table and that protected routes are enforced server-side (middleware).

checks.question: Is important data backed up, and are database changes made through migrations?
checks.evidence: `supabase/migrations` exists, so schema changes are versioned. The README mentions manual 1-click JSON export/import. No scheduled database backup is documented.
checks.next_step: Document the Supabase backup or point-in-time recovery setup and a restore procedure.

checks.question: Are third-party packages reasonably up to date and free of known security problems?
checks.evidence: Not checked: the dependency audit was not run and nothing was installed. Both `package-lock.json` and `yarn.lock` are present, which is ambiguous.
checks.next_step: Delete one lockfile, then run `npm audit` and update outdated packages.

checks.question: If it breaks while people use it, will logs or alerts show what happened?
checks.evidence: The scan found only 7 logging matches in 7 files, and there is no sign of error tracking or alerting such as Sentry. There is no CI or deploy config.
checks.next_step: Add an error tracker such as Sentry and basic structured logging for server routes.

checks.question: Does it stay fast with realistic amounts of data and users?
checks.evidence: Not checked: no load or profiling evidence is available. The app is described as client-side with a 365-day heatmap and many views, and no pagination or memoization evidence is visible.
checks.next_step: Test with a large seeded dataset (thousands of tasks and habit logs) and profile the Kanban, Gantt and heatmap views.

checks.question: Is there a written, repeatable way to deploy it and to roll back a bad release?
checks.evidence: The CI/deploy file list is empty, so there is no pipeline, no deploy documentation and no rollback procedure.
checks.next_step: Add a CI workflow for lint and build, and a `DEPLOY.md` covering Vercel deploys and rollback to a previous deployment.

checks.question: Could someone new run it and understand it from the docs alone?
checks.evidence: `README.md` describes features in detail. Most other docs are agent skill files under `.agents/skills/`, not app docs. The visible README has no setup, env var or architecture sections.
checks.next_step: Add setup, environment variables, architecture overview and contributing notes to `README.md`.

readiness.method: Static evidence only; tests, build and audit were not run in this pass.

debug_playbook.symptom: AI quick add or voice entry does nothing or gives wrong results
steps: Check that the Groq key is set for the server.
Look at the server route to see whether it returns an error.
Check whether the app fell back to the offline helper.
Try the sample phrase scripts in scratch to compare results.

debug_playbook.symptom: Data saves on screen but is missing after reload or on another device
steps: Confirm Supabase is configured.
Check whether changes are stuck in the offline queue.
Look at the store's save logic for that data type.
Use the scratch table count scripts to see if rows reached the cloud.

debug_playbook.symptom: New account cannot sign in, has no profile or shows wrong starting values
steps: Check that both migrations were applied.
Check the row-level security rules are not blocking access.
Review the sign-up and guest logic in the auth store.
Compare with the fresh account test in scratch.

debug_playbook.symptom: A score, grade average or analytics number looks wrong
steps: Find the helper that calculates the number.
Check the raw data it reads in the store.
Note the grade math uses a 10 point scale weighted by credits.
Check the screen is showing the helper's result directly.

debug_playbook.symptom: The app does not build or start
steps: Read the error message for the failing file.
Check the run commands in package.json.
Check that the libraries are installed.
Look at the TypeScript settings files that tsconfig.json points to, which are not listed here.

glossary.meaning: The web framework the app is built on.
The online database service that stores the user's data in the cloud.
The AI service used to understand typed sentences and transcribe speech.
The central place in the app where all the user's data is held while the app runs.
A database rule that lets each user see only their own records.
A database setup script that creates or changes tables.
Shared named values for colors and sizes so the look stays consistent.
A styling tool that applies looks through short class names.
A user type (student, professional or builder) that changes the app's wording.
Experience points earned for actions, used for levels and achievements.
